title: TerraTofu GUI project (.ttg.json)
description: A cloud-architecture diagram: settings, containers, nodes, edges and views. Written by TerraTofu GUI; readable by `ttg` and any MCP client.

views.description: Saved canvas views (filters). Optional; absent in files written by older versions.

provider_settings.description:
Values for provider-level variables declared in `definitions/providers/*.toml`
(region, location, subscription id, ...).

state_encryption.description:
OpenTofu-only: emit a state `encryption` block. Terraform has none, so there it
only produces a warning.

state_encryption_key.description:
Id of the `encryption_key` entity whose key encrypts the state (AWS KMS / Google
Cloud KMS key provider). The key cannot live in the configuration whose state it
encrypts, so the export moves it to the separate `bootstrap/` root. Unset, or on a
provider without a KMS key provider, the state is encrypted with a passphrase.

provider_versions.description:
Per-provider version constraint for `required_providers` (`{ "aws": "~> 6.0" }`).
A provider without an entry uses its definition's `version_constraint`.

tags.description:
Tags applied to every resource the project generates (cost allocation, ownership).
How they reach the HCL is the provider definition's business: AWS `default_tags`,
GCP `default_labels`, Azure a `tags` argument merged into each resource.

kubernetes_manifests.description:
Also write a `k8s/` directory of Kubernetes manifests beside the Terraform: per
workload a Namespace, ServiceAccount, Deployment, Service, volumes and autoscaling,
filled in from `terraform output` by a small render script. Off by default; left
out of the file while off so older projects do not change on save.

cost_assumptions.description:
Usage assumptions behind the cost estimate (`ttg_codegen::cost`): project-wide
values and per-entity overrides. Empty means every default.

cost_currency.description: Also show cost estimates in this currency, at a fixed rate. Prices are USD.

environments.description:
Named environments (`pilot`, `prod`), in order. Empty: the project has none and
exports exactly as before. Entities override field values per environment
(`overrides`); the export keeps one root per provider, with a `.tfvars` and a
state key per environment (see `crate::environment`).

name_prefix.description:
Put in front of every generated resource name (`zipos-${var.environment}` gives
`zipos-staging-db`), so environments can share one account. May use project
variables, `${var.environment}` among them.

variables.description:
Project variables: declared once, used in any field value as `${var.<name>}`,
with a value per environment (see `crate::environment`).

Tool.description:
Which IaC tool the project targets. Codegen differences between the two are confined
to `ttg-codegen::tool`.

BackendConfig.description:
Where the state lives. Rendered into the `terraform {}` block by `ttg-codegen::state`,
which also owns the list of backend types and the keys each one takes (`s3`: `bucket`,
`region`, optional `key_prefix`, `key` and `kms_key_id`; `azurerm`:
`resource_group_name`, `storage_account_name`, `container_name`, optional `key_prefix`
and `key`; `gcs`: `bucket`, optional `key_prefix` (or its own name, `prefix`); `local`:
optional `path`). The state key is derived — `<key_prefix>/terraform.tfstate` — so a
named environment can later slot in between; an explicit `key` gets it in front of its
file name.

CostAssumptions.description:
Usage assumptions behind the cost estimate, keyed by assumption name
(`bucket_gb`, `pool_node_hours_per_day`, …; `ttg_codegen::cost::ASSUMPTIONS` lists
them with their defaults). A key that is absent takes the estimator's default, so an
empty value is the common case and is not written to the file.

entities.description:
Per-entity overrides: entity id → assumption → value, e.g. one bucket that holds
two terabytes of recordings. They win over `values`. Entries for entities that no
longer exist are ignored.

DisplayCurrency.description:
Show estimates in another currency too. Prices are bundled in US dollars; this is a
fixed rate the user sets and dates, never fetched.

code.description: ISO code shown next to the converted figures, e.g. `GBP`.

rate.description: Units of `code` per US dollar, e.g. `0.75`.

date.description: When the rate was taken, free text (e.g. `2026-09-29`), shown beside it.

ProjectVariable.description:
A project variable: declared once in the settings, used in field values as
`${var.<name>}`, given a value per environment. Where the values differ the export
declares it as a Terraform variable of the same name, set in each environment's
`.tfvars`; where they do not, the value is written in place.

value.description: The value outside any environment, and in every environment without its own.

Container.description: A resource that can hold other resources (VPC, Resource Group, Project).

providers.description: Providers this container is part of (empty = every provider).

extra.description: Extra provider arguments beyond what the mapping sets (schema-validated).

classification.description: How sensitive the data it holds is; absent = not classified.

overrides.description:
Field values that differ per named environment (`settings.environments`):
environment -> the values replacing `config` / `provider_config` there.

Position.description: Canvas position in world units (pixels at zoom 1.0). Stored as integers.

Classification.description:
How sensitive the data a resource holds (or handles) is. Documentation today —
views filter on it and "Where personal data goes" is built from it — and the key
posture rules will read later. Absent means "not classified", not "public".

oneOf.description: Personal data (GDPR's sense): anything that identifies a person or is about one.
Payment card or bank data (PCI scope).

EnvOverride.description:
What one environment changes on one entity. A value here replaces the entity's own
value for that field in that environment; a field without one keeps the base value.
An override cannot remove a value, only replace it.

config.description: Abstract field values, as in the entity's `config`.

provider_config.description: Provider field values, as in the entity's `provider_config`.

absent.description:
The entity does not exist in this environment: it, and every link to and from it,
is left out there (a container's contents move up to its parent).

Node.description: A leaf resource on the canvas.

size.description: Custom node size; absent means the default node size.

manual.description: User-declared "this resource exists already / will be created by hand".

providers.description:
Providers this entity is part of (empty = every provider). A provider layer is
the abstract graph minus entities not tagged for it; see `Project::layer`.

extra.description: Extra provider arguments beyond what the mapping sets (schema-validated).

classification.description: How sensitive the data it holds is; absent = not classified.

description.description:
Why this resource exists. An HCL comment above its blocks, and a `Description`
tag where the provider's tags can hold one (see `ttg_codegen::emit`).

owner.description: Who looks after it: a team or a person. Emitted as an `Owner` tag / `owner` label.

overrides.description:
Field values that differ per named environment (`settings.environments`):
environment -> the values replacing `config` / `provider_config` there.

layout.description: Optional manual routing (which side of each node the line attaches to).

providers.description: Providers this link is part of (empty = every provider).

environments.description:
Named environments this link is part of (empty = every environment), so prod's
second route table can take over a subnet that pilot routes through the first.

Relation.description:
Kinds of relationship an edge can express. Direction is always
*source depends on / references target*.

oneOf.description:
Source is attached to / registered with target (route table -> subnet,
load balancer -> instance, function -> its backing storage).
Source publishes messages to target (function -> queue).

Source reads target's value (function -> secret, database -> password secret,
secret -> database endpoint).
Source writes its logs to target (function -> log group).
Source is encrypted at rest with target's key (bucket -> encryption key).
Messages the source could not deliver go to target (queue -> dead-letter queue).

Source makes requests of target (service to service). Documentation only: no
mapping generates anything for it, it adds no `depends_on` and no manual step,
and it stays out of the dependency graph so two services may call each other.

EdgeLayout.description: Where an edge attaches to its endpoints. Absent means automatic.

Anchor.description: One end of an edge: a side of the node and an offset along it.

offset.description: Position along the side as a percentage from -100 (start) to 100 (end); 0 = centre.

View.description:
A named, saved view shown as a tab above the canvas: a filter (what is shown), an
optional layout of its own (where things are), and annotations (groups, flows,
notes, logical nodes) that document it.

description.description: What this view is for, shown under the view bar and in its exported document.

layout.description: `Some` = this view positions things itself; `None` = shares the All layout.

legend.description: Show the legend panel over the canvas.

ViewFilter.description:
A saved canvas filter: which entities and links are shown. Purely visual; codegen
always sees the whole project.

focus.description: Only show entities within `depth` links of this one (plus their containers).

only.description:
When non-empty, show only these entities (plus their containers). Used by
"show this path" in the reachability overlay.

containers.description:
Draw containers (networks, resource groups, vaults). Off for architecture maps
that group things their own way.

providers.description: Only entities on these provider layers (empty = every layer).

origin.description: Curated types only, native (raw schema) types only, or both.

types.description: Only these abstract type ids (empty = all).

name_glob.description: Case-insensitive `*` / `?` glob on the display name (empty = all).

hide_edges.description:
Hide the structural links, so a view shows only its data-flow arrows.
`hide_links` is accepted as a spelling of the same flag: agents reach for it,
and a filter that silently dropped the key would draw the wrong picture.

classifications.description: Only entities classified as one of these (empty = all, classified or not).

Origin.description: Where a resource came from: the curated catalog or the raw provider schema.

oneOf.description: Only types from the curated catalog.

ViewLayout.description:
Positions and sizes a view keeps separately from the shared layout. Entities not
listed use the shared position, so an empty layout is "same as All, until moved".

Group.description:
A grouping box drawn on a view: pure annotation, never exported. Entities are "in"
a group when their centre lies inside its box; dragging the group takes them along.

color.description: `#rrggbb`; a default palette colour when absent.

Flow.description:
A labelled data-flow arrow on a view: architecture-map annotation, never exported
and never a dependency.

step.description: Position in the sequence, drawn as a badge at the arrow's start.

color.description: `#rrggbb`; the default ink colour when absent.

data.description:
What travels along it, in words ("call audio", "card token"): drawn under the
label and listed in the exports. Free text; the label says what happens, this
says what it happens to.

FlowEnd.description: One end of a data-flow arrow: a resource, a group or a logical node.

Note.description:
A note box on a view: a title and a wrapped body explaining part of the picture.
Never exported. With an `anchor` it is drawn beside what it explains and `position`
is the offset from that thing's top-right corner; without one, `position` is the
note's own place on the canvas.

NoteAnchor.description: What a note points at: anything a flow can attach to, or a flow itself.

Logical.description:
An annotation-only node on a view: something the diagram does not (and should not)
generate — a browser, a third-party API, one workload inside a cluster. Never
exported; flows may start and end at it, and it belongs to groups geometrically
like a resource does.

icon.description: Short text drawn in the icon block, e.g. `WEB`.
